general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **US-Iran Relations:** On Friday, June 27, 2026, the United States launched retaliatory air strikes against Iran, targeting missile and drone storage locations and coastal radar sites after Iran used a drone to strike the Singapore-flagged cargo ship MV Ever Lovely in the Strait of Hormuz on June 25. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps subsequently retaliated with attacks against US military installations in the region and Bahrain. This exchange of strikes severely tested a fragile interim ceasefire reached by the two nations just one week prior, reigniting tensions in the critical international shipping lane. Escalations in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil transit chokepoint, pose significant risks to global energy markets and international maritime security.

• **Venezuela Earthquakes:** The confirmed death toll from twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, 2026, has risen to 1,430, with tens of thousands of residents still unaccounted for across collapsed northern coastal towns including La Guaira state. The powerful 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude tremors, striking within less than a minute of each other, caused severe damage to 383 buildings and displaced 3,007 people who are now in temporary shelters. Rescue efforts are racing against time, with the UN Humanitarian Agency estimating over 50,000 people are missing, and critical scarcity of heavy machinery forcing local volunteers to dig through rubble with bare hands. This unfolding tragedy represents a significant humanitarian crisis requiring urgent international aid and support for a country already facing economic fragility.

• **Israel-Lebanon Framework Deal:** On Friday, June 27, 2026, Lebanon and Israel signed a US-sponsored "framework deal" in Washington, D.C., concluding the fifth round of negotiations between the two sides. The agreement, facilitated by a US mediator, affirms a shared goal of achieving "lasting peace and security" and declares an "ambition to end conflict between them, ensure the sovereignty and security of both countries, and establish peaceful neighborly relations." While heralded by the US as a "first step" toward peace, Hezbollah, a significant non-state actor in Lebanon, rejected the agreement, raising questions about its enforceability and the potential for renewed internal conflict. This deal attempts to de-escalate a long-standing regional conflict, but Hezbollah's rejection highlights persistent challenges to stability and potential for further geopolitical complications in the Middle East.

• **EU Policy on Ukrainian Refugees:** On Friday, June 27, 2026, the European Commission proposed to extend its temporary protection scheme for Ukrainian refugees until March 2028, but explicitly blocked newly arriving military-age men (aged 23 to 60) from obtaining this status. This policy shift aims to support Kyiv's mobilization needs by excluding individuals who leave Ukraine without legal military authorization. While those already granted temporary protection will retain their status, this proposal, which needs approval by a qualified majority of EU member states, will significantly impact future Ukrainian male refugees seeking asylum in Europe. This decision reflects a shifting European stance on refugee policy in the context of ongoing conflict, potentially influencing international humanitarian law and the future demographic and military landscape of Ukraine.

Why it matters: Today's top stories reveal a volatile global landscape characterized by escalating geopolitical tensions, profound humanitarian crises requiring immediate international attention, and significant policy shifts that will redefine regional stability and international norms.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Figma:** Figma launched Code Layers, enabling teams to integrate executable code directly onto the design canvas, and Generative Plugins, allowing users to create custom tools by describing them in plain language. These features significantly bridge the gap between design and development workflows, moving beyond previous manual handoff processes. A developer can now directly clone a Git repository into Figma to edit code-backed components and sync changes, or a designer can create a custom plugin to automate a repetitive task without writing any code.

• **Perplexity AI:** Perplexity released Computer integration within Microsoft 365 applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams), bringing AI workflows directly into these productivity tools. This update allows users to perform deep research, analyze documents, and generate content with inline citations and sources without leaving their M365 environment. A knowledge worker can now prompt Perplexity within Excel to analyze a quarterly workbook, identify key revenue changes, and summarize the drivers, with all figures cited back to the source sheet.

• **Adobe Creative Cloud:** Adobe rolled out significant AI updates across its Creative Cloud suite, including AI-assisted culling and a new Photo to Video feature in Lightroom, and an offline-capable Remove Tool in Photoshop. The Lightroom enhancements streamline photo selection by evaluating individuals in photos for open and sharp eyes, and the Photo to Video feature leverages Firefly and Google Veo to turn still images into dynamic video clips. A photographer can now use Lightroom's AI to quickly identify the best shots from a large event and then generate b-roll video from a still image for social media, while a designer can use Photoshop's Remove Tool to instantly erase an object from an image even without an internet connection.

• **Cursor:** Cursor introduced major improvements to Automations and Cloud Environment Setup, allowing developers to create always-on AI agents for repetitive tasks and establish cloud-based development environments in under 10 minutes. The Automations feature includes a new `/automate` skill and expanded triggers for GitHub and Slack, while the Cloud Environment Setup captures reusable snapshots for faster agent spin-up and testing. A developer can now use a plain language prompt to create an automation that monitors GitHub pull requests and generates summaries, or rapidly provision a consistent cloud dev environment for a new project in minutes.

Why it matters: The AI landscape is maturing rapidly, moving from standalone models to deeply integrated, workflow-changing tools that blur the lines between traditional software categories and AI agents.

investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS
*   **Oil & Gas — WTI Oil:** WTI crude oil prices have fallen to three-month lows and even pre-Iran war levels, driven by easing supply concerns from the Middle East. This includes increased shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz, progress in Middle East ceasefire negotiations, and QatarEnergy issuing a crude tender for July-August signaling higher supply. Additionally, OPEC+ countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, decided to increase their oil production cap by 188,000 barrels per day in June, further contributing to the supply increase. This sustained increase in supply and de-escalation of geopolitical tensions reduces the risk premium on oil.
*   **Equities & Indices — Tech / Magnificent 7 (Apple & Microsoft):** Apple's stock dropped significantly after the company announced price increases of 15-25% on various MacBook and iPad models, citing surging AI-driven memory and storage chip costs. Microsoft also increased prices for its Xbox consoles due to similar rising component costs and is facing investor scrutiny over substantial capital expenditure for AI, impacting its free cash flow profile. These actions are raising concerns about potential demand destruction and the profitability of AI investments across the tech sector.
*   **Equities & Indices — Nasdaq 100 / Big Tech:** The Nasdaq 100 and broader tech sector continue to experience a sell-off as investors grow increasingly skeptical about lofty artificial intelligence valuations, rising interest rates, and the massive spending required for AI infrastructure. This ongoing sentiment shift, following a period of significant gains, is leading to profit-taking and a re-evaluation of growth stock prospects.
*   **FinTech & Digital Payments — FINX ETF:** The Global X FinTech ETF (FINX) declared a dividend of $0.0429 per share on June 26, 2026, payable on July 7, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 29, 2026. This dividend announcement, alongside a generally positive outlook for global FinTech revenue growth and increased US FinTech funding in Q1 2026, may be contributing to positive sentiment in the sector.

Why it matters: The shifting dynamics in the tech sector, particularly the impact of rising AI-related costs on hardware pricing and company profitability, are fueling a broader re-evaluation of AI valuations and creating headwinds for long-term tech investors.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Prestação Social Única (PSU):** O Parlamento aprovou em 25 de junho a criação da Prestação Social Única, que consolidará 13 apoios sociais não contributivos dispersos num único benefício. Anteriormente, existiam múltiplos apoios sociais fragmentados; agora, haverá uma prestação de natureza diferencial, calculada como a diferença entre um montante global (com valor de referência do Indexante dos Apoios Sociais - IAS, atualmente €537,13) e os rendimentos do agregado familiar, sujeita a limites de rendimento e património (máximo de 60 IAS para património mobiliário e bens móveis sujeitos a registo). Para adultos em idade ativa, o acesso implica a disponibilidade para trabalho ou atividades de solidariedade social. A medida entra em vigor em agosto de 2026. A simplificação do sistema social pode facilitar o acesso a apoios para as famílias mais vulneráveis, mas introduz condicionalidades de trabalho social.

• **Reforma do Código dos Contratos Públicos:** O Conselho de Ministros aprovou em 25 de junho um Decreto-Lei que reforma o Código dos Contratos Públicos (CCP). Esta revisão moderniza e simplifica o regime da contratação pública, visando reduzir a burocracia, aumentar a transparência e promover uma contratação mais orientada para resultados, com foco na digitalização. Anteriormente, os processos de contratação pública eram frequentemente criticados pela sua complexidade; agora, espera-se que os procedimentos sejam mais ágeis e eficientes. A medida visa tornar o investimento público mais eficiente e acelerar a execução de projetos estratégicos, beneficiando empresas que participam em concursos públicos.

• **Regime Jurídico do Contrato de Aproveitamento Energético Renovável:** A Lei n.º 29/2026, de 23 de junho, cria o regime jurídico do contrato de aproveitamento energético renovável (CAER). Esta lei permite que os proprietários cedam os direitos de aproveitamento energético dos seus imóveis (como solos urbanos não construídos, telhados ou terraços) e estabelece o deferimento tácito para o licenciamento de unidades de produção para autoconsumo (UPAC) a partir de fontes renováveis. Previamente, o licenciamento de UPAC podia ser mais demorado; agora, a aprovação é tácita após determinado prazo, e novos modelos contratuais são instituídos para a partilha de custos e receitas da energia produzida. A medida impulsiona a produção descentralizada de eletricidade a partir de energias renováveis, oferecendo novas oportunidades para proprietários e investidores.

• **Novo Regime de IVA de Grupo:** Entra em vigor em 1 de julho de 2026 o novo regime de IVA de grupo, introduzido pela Lei n.º 62/2025. Este regime permite que empresas relacionadas sejam tratadas como uma única entidade para efeitos de IVA, possibilitando a compensação de saldos de IVA entre membros do grupo e eliminando a tributação de transações internas. Anteriormente, cada empresa geria o seu IVA individualmente; agora, grupos económicos com vínculos financeiros, económicos e organizacionais (onde a empresa-mãe detém pelo menos 75% do capital e controla mais de 50% dos direitos de voto) podem consolidar a sua posição de IVA. A medida simplifica as obrigações fiscais e melhora a liquidez para os grupos empresariais.

• **Pacote Fiscal da Habitação – IVA a 6%:** A taxa reduzida de IVA de 6% para empreitadas de construção e reabilitação de imóveis destinados a habitação própria permanente ou arrendamento habitacional, conforme o Decreto-Lei n.º 97/2026 (publicado a 20 de maio de 2026), arranca em julho de 2026. Esta medida aplica-se a operações urbanísticas iniciadas entre 25 de setembro de 2025 e 31 de dezembro de 2029, com exigibilidade do imposto a partir de 1 de janeiro de 2026 (com retroatividade possível mediante acordo). Anteriormente, estas obras estariam sujeitas às taxas gerais de IVA; agora, beneficiam de uma redução significativa. Para habitação própria permanente, o imóvel deve ser vendido no prazo máximo de 24 meses após a licença de utilização; o não cumprimento resulta num agravamento de 10% do IMT, não na reversão do IVA. Esta medida visa reduzir os custos de construção e reabilitação, incentivando o aumento da oferta de habitação e tornando-a mais acessível.

Why it matters: As aprovações recentes na Assembleia da República e no Conselho de Ministros, juntamente com medidas fiscais que entram em vigor em julho, sinalizam uma simplificação da burocracia na contratação pública e no setor energético, bem como incentivos fiscais significativos para o mercado da habitação e uma reestruturação fundamental dos apoios sociais.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Tax Simplification Package (Directive on Administrative Cooperation Recast):** The European Commission adopted this package on June 24, 2026, aiming to cut red tape and reduce costs for businesses across the EU. Previously, Member States had discretion over the EBITDA cap for deducting borrowing costs and the €3 million safe harbour was not uniformly mandatory. Now, a uniform and mandatory 30% EBITDA cap is imposed across the EU for deducting exceeding borrowing costs, and Member States are mandated to implement a €3 million safe harbour for these deductions, with annual inflation indexation. Businesses operating across the EU, including Portuguese firms, must comply with these harmonised direct tax rules, which are expected to save EU businesses approximately €69 million per year by effectively removing smaller entities from the scope of the Interest Limitation Rule. Member States have 3 years to introduce the safe harbour.

• **Regulation (EU) 2026/1386 on the screening of foreign investments in the Union:** Published in the Official Journal on June 25, 2026, this Regulation by the European Parliament and the Council establishes a new framework for Member States to screen foreign direct investments into the Union on grounds of security or public order. This regulation repeals the previous Regulation (EU) 2019/452, enhancing and clarifying the screening process. Previously, the framework was less defined; now, Member States are required to implement more robust screening mechanisms to mitigate risks to critical assets, technologies, and infrastructure. This will lead to increased scrutiny and potentially more complex due diligence for foreign investors, including Portuguese entities investing outside Portugal but within the EU.

• **Regulation (EU) 2026/1388 on plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques:** This Regulation, adopted by the European Parliament and the Council and published in the Official Journal on June 25, 2026, establishes a new regulatory framework for plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques (NGTs) and their products. Previously, NGT plants were largely subject to the same strict regulations as genetically modified organisms (GMOs). The new rule introduces a differentiated approach, particularly for NGT plants that could also occur naturally or through conventional breeding, making their development and marketing less burdensome. This will significantly impact agricultural businesses, biotech companies, and food producers in Portugal and across the EU by fostering innovation in plant breeding and potentially contributing to sustainable agriculture.

• **Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/1383 amending Council Regulation (EC) No 338/97 (CITES):** Published in the Official Journal on June 25, 2026, this Commission Regulation amends Council Regulation (EC) No 338/97 to reflect the latest updates to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Previously, EU trade rules for endangered species were based on older versions of the CITES appendices. Now, the updated appendices, agreed at the 20th Conference of the Parties and by the Scientific Review Group, will govern trade restrictions and requirements for listed species. This impacts businesses involved in the trade of wild fauna and flora or their derivatives, including those in Portugal, by altering their compliance obligations to align with global biodiversity conservation efforts.

Why it matters: The adoption of the Tax Simplification Package represents a significant step towards harmonising direct tax rules and reducing administrative burden for businesses across the EU, directly impacting investors and financial markets.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **"Lulu's Law" Enacted:** President Trump signed S. 1003, known as "Lulu's Law," into law on June 26, 2026, mandating that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) issue an order explicitly permitting the transmission of wireless emergency alerts to mobile phones in the event of a shark attack. Previously, explicit FCC permission for such alerts for shark attacks was not federally mandated; now, the FCC is required to allow these transmissions. This action broadens the scope of emergency alert system usage for public safety.

• **U.S. Conducts Strikes in Iran:** On Friday, June 26, 2026, the United States conducted military strikes against missile and drone locations and coastal radar sites in Iran in response to a drone attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. This represents a direct military enforcement action, escalating tensions following a drone attack a day earlier. Previously, these specific Iranian sites were not targeted by U.S. military action in response to this incident; now, they have been struck.

• **U.S. Treasury Sanctions Networks in Sudan Civil War:** On June 27, 2026, the U.S. Treasury Department blacklisted eight individuals and entities for supporting procurement and recruitment networks supplying both sides of Sudan's civil war. This action prohibits U.S. persons from dealing with these designated individuals and entities. Previously, these specific networks were not subject to U.S. sanctions; now, they are designated, tightening economic pressure to curtail the conflict.

• **OFAC Delists Three Russian Nationals:** Effective June 23, 2026, and reported on June 27, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) removed three Russian nationals—Anton Alekseevich Krugovov, Tamara Aleksandrovna Topchi, and Natalya Vladislavovna Puzyrnikova—from its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List). Previously, these individuals were subject to U.S. sanctions, prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in transactions with them and blocking their property; now, their property is unblocked, and U.S. persons are no longer prohibited from dealing with them.

• **CBP Issues Interim Final Rule on Informal International Mail Entries:** U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) published an interim final rule on June 26, 2026, establishing that, effective July 24, 2026, only parties with the right to make entry or licensed customs brokers will be allowed to file informal international mail entries for shipments valued under $2,500. Previously, other parties could potentially file these entries; now, stricter requirements are in place to ensure compliance and control over lower-value international shipments.

Why it matters: The U.S. government took significant steps this week in both national security responses, through military action and new sanctions, and domestic regulatory adjustments, reflecting active policy implementation across various sectors.
